# ROOT CAUSE — READY OPEN CODE EXISTS; EXECUTION PATH WAS WRONG

Fresh investigation result:

1. The required local-edit mechanism already exists as mature OSS: `lquesada/ComfyUI-Inpaint-CropAndStitch`. Its `Inpaint Stitch` explicitly restores the edited crop into the original image while leaving unmasked areas untouched; unmasked pixels do not pass through VAE encode/decode.
2. Current Shared HQ already has a `ComfyUIBackend` that targets a real ComfyUI HTTP server (`/system_stats`, `/prompt`, `/history/{id}`, `/view`) with default `comfyui_url = http://127.0.0.1:8188`.
3. However current main workflow `salvador-production-image-edit.json` is still only a disposable smoke workflow: `LoadImage -> ImageInvert -> SaveImage`. It is NOT an inpaint/edit workflow.
4. The present ChatGPT execution container has no ComfyUI installation, no model weights, no NVIDIA runtime/GPU, and PyTorch reports CPU-only. Therefore this chat cannot execute the ready ComfyUI workflow locally.
5. No connected ComfyUI app/plugin is exposed in this session. The available image generation tool is a different engine and does not expose the exact ComfyUI crop/mask/stitch contract; using it caused repeated full-frame redraws.

Therefore the blocker is NOT missing algorithm/code. It is an EXECUTION/BRIDGE mismatch:

`READY OSS + READY ZORR BACKEND != LIVE COMFYUI RUNTIME AVAILABLE TO THIS SESSION`

Hard prevention law:
- `CUSTOM_CODE = 0`
- Do not call whole-image generation for HARD PROBLEM #001.
- Do not claim `MASKED_EDIT_PASS` unless execution comes from a real ComfyUI runtime with a crop/inpaint/stitch workflow and a fresh verification that unmasked pixels are byte-identical/pixel-identical outside the declared mask.
- Reuse the existing owner-PC ComfyUI endpoint/controller path; replace only the disposable workflow asset with an upstream ready workflow or equivalent graph assembled from upstream nodes. No replacement implementation.

Recommended ready stack:
`OWNER LOCKED PNG + explicit edit mask + InpaintCropImproved + InpaintModelConditioning + existing inpaint sampler/model + InpaintStitchImproved`, optionally with existing ControlNet/OpenPose/rig-derived pose condition for arms-down.

Truth status:
`OPEN_CODE_GAP = NO`
`ALGORITHM_GAP = NO`
`CURRENT_CHAT_LOCAL_COMFYUI_RUNTIME = NO`
`CURRENT_MAIN_PRODUCTION_INPAINT_WORKFLOW = NO`
`EXECUTION_BRIDGE_TO_OWNER_PC_COMFYUI = REQUIRED`

# ZORR BLATT — CHARACTER GEOMETRY MODEL V1

STATUS = MATHEMATICAL BASIS CANDIDATE

## HARD CORRECTION

`PIXELS ARE OBSERVATIONS, NOT CHARACTER PHYSICS.`

A raster image is the end of the chain:

`CHARACTER INTRINSICS -> POSE/DEFORMATION -> CAMERA/PROJECTION -> APPEARANCE/LIGHT -> RASTERIZATION`

The source PNG/JPG is evidence about those latent variables; it is not the physical model itself.

## STRUCTURED CHARACTER STATE

Use latent state

`Theta = {T, G0, J, B, W, R, M}`

where:
- `T` = topology / semantic adjacency;
- `G0` = rest geometry / morphology;
- `J` = semantic joint graph;
- `B` = intrinsic bone lengths / morphometric ratios;
- `W` = deformation/skinning weights;
- `R` = semantic regions (skin/hair/garments/etc.);
- `M` = identity-critical markings/material maps.

Pose is separate: `q`.
Camera is separate: `C`.
ZORR appearance/style is separate: `A`.
Lighting is separate: `L`.

Observed image:

`I = Rasterize(Project_C(Render(D(Theta,q), A, L)))`

For pose normalization, preserve `Theta` and change `q` only.

## FITTING LAW

Do not optimize against raw RGB alone.

Use hierarchical constrained fitting:

`E_total = lambda_landmark E_landmark + lambda_shape E_shape + lambda_sil E_SDF + lambda_ratio E_morphometric + lambda_rigid E_ARAP + lambda_region E_regions + lambda_camera E_projection + small_lambda_rgb E_photometric`

Accepted Character Truth remains hard-constrained.

## SCALE-FREE / PROJECTION LAW

Physical proportions are dimensionless ratios or world/body coordinates, not pixels.
Use normalized landmark configurations / Procrustes-style alignment before shape comparison.

World/body, camera/view, normalized projection and screen pixels are distinct spaces.
A screen-space pixel delta cannot be treated as a physical body delta without the camera model.

## SILHOUETTE LAW

Silhouette is projected shape evidence only.
Use contour correspondences / shape descriptors and SDF boundary error after camera alignment.
Never use one silhouette to invent hidden body volume.

## DEFORMATION LAW

Preferred critical path:
- existing ZORR Character DNA / parametric humanoid driver;
- semantic skeleton;
- target base pose at the joint-transform level;
- Babylon/native rig path;
- local-rigidity preservation where needed (ARAP / bounded biharmonic weights); avoid known matrix-blend collapse near joints when it materially affects the result.

## BASE POSE

`COMMON BASE POSE != COMMON BODY`

Base presentation:
- front;
- upright / at-attention;
- arms down and readable;
- hands visible;
- no weapon;
- white background.

Each character preserves its own `Theta`.

## SALVADOR ROLE

SALVADOR must not infer character physics by unconstrained free image regeneration.

ZORR math/rig produces locked geometry/pose/silhouette/depth/region conditions.
SALVADOR renders/normalizes appearance under internal ZORR visual law while respecting those conditions.

## PIXEL DOMAIN — LEGAL USE

Pixels remain valid for final projection/render QC: line thickness at declared scale, mask overlap, edge density, tone bands, raster contour residual and texture-frequency analysis.

`PIXEL QC != PHYSICAL MODEL`

## UNDERDETERMINATION

If a single 2D view cannot prove hidden geometry:

`HIDDEN_GEOMETRY = NOT_PROVEN`

Resolve only through additional approved views or existing ZORR parametric/Character DNA truth.

## TECHNICAL RESEARCH BASIS

- inverse graphics: infer structured physical variables that can reproduce the observation;
- Kendall/Procrustes shape spaces: compare shape after factoring irrelevant translation/rotation/scale;
- Shape Contexts + regularized TPS: contour correspondence and alignment;
- SDF/level-set representation: boundary as zero level-set, useful for geometric boundary loss;
- libigl ARAP: deformation that strives to preserve local distances/angles;
- bounded biharmonic weights: smooth nonnegative partition-of-unity skeleton/handle weights;
- dual-quaternion skinning: addresses collapse/shrink artifacts of linear matrix blending near joints;
- Babylon skeletons: hierarchical bones with transformation matrices and per-vertex weights;
- PyTorch3D camera model: explicit separation of world/view/NDC/screen coordinate systems.

`/ZORR/PERMANENT_ARCHIVE_V1/PRODUCTION_LAWS/CHARACTER_GEOMETRY/ZORR_CHARACTER_GEOMETRY_MODEL_V1.md`
